title: DTCR cross-repository Expand & Contract (R2) receipt
description: The terminal statement of one cross-repository Expand & Contract run: which states of the five-phase protocol were actually entered, which repositories took part and on what kind of edge, what the dual-run and telemetry window observed, what the downstream inventory found, and which of the three terminals the run reached. The three are kept apart because they are three different facts a summary flattens into one word. CONTRACTION_CANDIDATE means every consumer receipt is bound and every observation lane ran and agreed; BLOCKED names which link of the chain was never reached, most often because a declared contract adapter has no implementation to run or a registry publication needs an authority this protocol does not hold; ROLLED_BACK means traffic had moved, a lane disagreed, and a named phase in a named repository was put back. Nothing here establishes that anything was applied to a real codebase, that a real consumer took traffic, or that the legacy surface may be removed; contraction, publication and merge are repository and Human authority.

participants.description: Every repository this run touched, and the fact that the ordering between them is a process edge. A cross-repository run with fewer than two participants is a single-repository refactor wearing this protocol's name.

states_entered.description: The states this run actually entered, not the states the protocol declares. A run that stopped at the provider and lists every state is reporting the diagram.

observation.description: What the E1 window observed, kept apart from what it authorises. `window_verdict` is a reading and NOT_OBSERVED is one of its values, because a window nobody watched is not a window that held.

samples.description: An error rate computed from an empty window is zero for the same reason a switched-off meter is.

contraction.description: Requested, counted, and never performed. The two counts are kept as two numbers rather than one ratio because the gate is `bound == required`, and a ratio rounds the one consumer nobody migrated into a percentage.

rollback_subjects.description: One restore point per phase entered, in the repository that phase writes. The obligation is per phase and not per run because a single 'roll back to this commit' names one repository, and the others are the ones left carrying the half-applied change.

rollback.description: Which phase in which repository was put back, and to what. There is deliberately no reason field: which lane disagreed is already in `observation` and `blocked_on`, and a second copy of that fact is a copy that can disagree with the first.

blocked_on.description: A closed list. An open string here would let a run block on a sentence, and a sentence cannot be counted across runs.

hard_blockers.description: Every hard blocker this protocol names, each pinned false. They are assertions of absence rather than an optional list of what happened, because a blocker that can be omitted is a blocker a receipt can be silent about, and silence reads downstream as absence anyway. BREAKING_CHANGE_BYPASSED_BY_CONFIG_WEAKENING: the compatibility check that would have failed was replaced by a looser rule category, or narrowed by excluding the paths that changed. SCHEMA_PUBLISHED_WITHOUT_EXACT_SOURCE: a registry artifact whose source is a moving label cannot be traced back to the bytes that produced it once the label moves. GENERATED_STUB_DRIFT: a consumer built against stubs generated from a different contract commit than the one this run expanded. PROVIDER_REMOVES_LEGACY_BEFORE_CONSUMER_MIGRATION: Expand & Contract is an order, and a run that contracts while a consumer is still calling the old surface has run it backwards. CONSUMER_SWITCH_WITHOUT_FALLBACK: traffic moved to the new surface with no fallback bound, so the first failure on the new path has nowhere to go. DUAL_RUN_WITHOUT_IDEMPOTENCY: every write in the comparison window happened twice, so the comparison is between two states the run itself created. TELEMETRY_ABSENCE_PROMOTED_TO_SUCCESS: nothing broke that anybody was watching is a statement about the watching. NO_REMAINING_CALLERS_IN_PARTIAL_INDEX: zero callers found in the part of the fleet that was indexed is not zero callers, and it is the number a contraction gate reads as permission. BSR_ACCOUNT_ACCESS_PROMOTED_TO_CONTENT_RIGHTS: being able to push to a registry is a capability; being allowed to publish that schema's content is a rights and terms question. AUTOMATIC_CONTRACTION_OR_MERGE: a bound receipt from every consumer and a clean window are inputs to the decision to delete the old surface, never the decision. FALSE_CROSS_REPO_GIT_PARENT: cross-repository order is a process edge, and writing it as Git ancestry invents a history neither repository has.

establishes.description: All three pinned false. This protocol has run over synthetic multi-repository fixtures: no repository was read or written, no registry was contacted, and no real consumer took traffic. The bounded real-consumer canary is a separate lane owned by a separate issue, and DTCR_CROSS_REPO_EXPAND_CONTRACT_READY is admitted against this issue's exit criteria by a person reading them together with that canary's own receipt -- never asserted by a run of the thing being admitted.

allOf.description: A candidate that names what it is blocked on is a blocked run reported as a candidate.
TELEMETRY_ABSENCE_PROMOTED_TO_SUCCESS, in its observation-window form. A candidate whose window was never observed is proposing the removal of a live surface on the strength of nobody having looked.
NO_REMAINING_CALLERS_IN_PARTIAL_INDEX. A candidate resting on a partial inventory, or on an inventory that still found callers, is proposing to delete a surface somebody is still calling.
BLOCKED with nothing named is indistinguishable downstream from a run nobody started.
ROLLED_BACK with no rollback record does not say which phase in which repository was put back, or to what, so nobody can check that it was.

A contraction candidate that also names what it is blocked on.
A contraction candidate whose observation window was never observed.
A contraction candidate resting on a downstream inventory that is only a partial lower bound.
A contraction candidate whose own inventory still found callers on the legacy surface.
A blocked run that names nothing it is blocked on.
A rolled-back run with no rollback record, so nobody can check which phase was put back or to what.
A receipt recording that the migration was applied on a real codebase.
A receipt recording that a real bounded consumer canary was observed.
